Dockerfile.text:
FROM node:22-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY slot.mjs book.mjs render.mjs server.mjs ./
RUN mkdir -p /data && chown node /data
USER node
ENV PORT=8080 STATE=/tmp/state.json TRUST_PROXY=false
EXPOSE 8080
HEALTHCHECK CMD wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz || exit 1
CMD ["node", "server.mjs"]

README.md.text:
# Slot Keeper

After using this, you can now **let people book time with you from a page you host yourself**, offering only the times you are really free, in each visitor's own time zone, with an invitation, a reminder and a cancel or reschedule link, instead of paying a scheduling service per seat or trading emails about times.

**Live tool:** https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/slot-keeper/

Two parts, both free and MIT:

- **`index.html`**: set weekly hours, buffers and notice, paste a calendar, and see the slots a visitor would get in any time zone. Runs in the browser; nothing is uploaded.
- **`server.mjs`**: one Node process, **zero dependencies**, state in one JSON file. Booking pages, JSON slots API, invitations, reminders, cancel and reschedule, admin, CSV export, a calendar feed of your bookings.

## Why someone would use this

| Today | Cost / catch | Slot Keeper |
|---|---|---|
| Calendly, SavvyCal, Acuity, Zoho Bookings | Priced per seat per month; invitee details live with them; multiple event types, buffers and reminders sit on paid tiers | Your server, unlimited event types and bookings, no seat fee |
| Cal.com and other open-source schedulers | Full platforms: a database, a build, integrations to configure | One Node process and one JSON file |
| "What times work for you?" emails | Slow, double-bookings, muddled time zones, no reminder | One link, only free times, invite and reminder included |

Honest limits: one host per booking page (no round-robin or team routing), it reads your calendar's busy time but does not write to it (subscribe to the bookings feed instead), no video-room creation (paste your meeting link as the location), no payments, no mobile app, one admin key. Recurring events in your calendar feed use the common rules (daily, weekly with days, monthly, yearly, with COUNT, UNTIL, INTERVAL and EXDATE). Rules like "first Monday of the month" count only their first occurrence; keep such a meeting as a day off in the event type.

## How it works

1. **Create an event type** at `/admin` (any user name, `ADMIN_KEY` as the password): name, length, weekly hours in your time zone (`mon-fri 09:00-12:00,13:00-17:00; sat 10:00-12:00`), buffers before and after, minimum notice, how many days ahead, an optional per-day limit, days off, and where it happens (a meeting link or address). You get the booking link `/b/<event>`, a link-or-iframe snippet and the JSON endpoint.
2. **Visitors pick a day and time** in their own zone (changeable on the page) and enter a name and email. Only times that are free *right now* can be booked: the server rechecks at booking, so two people cannot take the same slot, and a forged time is refused. Honeypot and a rate limit stop bots.
3. **Your busy time is respected.** Set `BUSY_ICS_URL` to your calendar's secret iCal address (Google Calendar: Settings, your calendar, "Secret address in iCal format"; Outlook and Apple Calendar have the same). It is read every five minutes, with recurring, all-day and different-zone events handled and daylight-saving changes kept. If the feed fails, the last good copy is used for an hour and `/admin` warns you; after that no times are offered at all, so nobody can book over a meeting you made elsewhere.
4. **Both sides get an invitation** with a calendar file (`METHOD:REQUEST`), a reminder goes out once before the booking (`REMINDER_HOURS`, default 24, `0` to turn off), and cancelling sends a calendar file that removes the entry. Each booking has a private link to cancel, add to calendar or **reschedule**: the old time is kept until the new one is confirmed.
5. **See bookings in your own calendar** by subscribing to `/feed/<secret>.ics` (shown on `/admin`).
6. **Housekeeping**: `RETENTION_DAYS` deletes old bookings; CSV export is spreadsheet-formula safe; `ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` (Slack/Discord) pings on bookings and cancellations; `EMBED_ORIGINS` lists the sites allowed to put the booking page in an iframe.

## Run it

```sh
cd ventures/slot-keeper
node --test        # no network
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) COMPANY_NAME=Acme DEFAULT_TZ=America/Denver node server.mjs
```

Email starts in **dry run**: bookings are saved but nothing is sent. To send, set `DRY_RUN=false`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `MAIL_FROM` (an address on a domain you verified with Resend, your own account) and `HOST_EMAIL` (where you want booking notices). `PUBLIC_URL` (https) is required when `DRY_RUN=false`: links in emails and reminders point at your domain, never at whatever Host header a stranger sends. Other settings: `STATE` (JSON file path; keep it on a persistent disk), `PORT`, `TRUST_PROXY=true` behind a proxy, `HIDE_SPONSOR_LINK=true`.

## One-click deploy

Fork the repository, then open `https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>`. Render builds the Dockerfile in **your** account with a 1 GB disk and generates `ADMIN_KEY`. Nothing runs on the author's accounts. Serve it over HTTPS only (Render does); the admin uses HTTP Basic auth. `docker-compose.yml` runs it on any box with Docker; Fly.io steps are at the top of `fly.toml`.

## Disclaimer

No warranty; no uptime or delivery guarantee. You operate the booking page and are responsible for the details it collects, your privacy notice, data-protection rules and your own email sending. Check the time and zone of every booking; a missed or double-booked appointment is your responsibility. Not legal, tax or financial advice. MIT licensed. If it saves you a subscription, you can [sponsor the author](https://github.com/sponsors/Duncan-Haywood).

VENTURE.yaml.text:
name: slot-keeper
description: >-
  Self-hosted booking pages (Calendly alternative): weekly hours, buffers,
  minimum notice, your calendar's busy time respected from a secret iCal feed
  (recurring and all-day events, time zones, daylight saving), slots shown in
  the visitor's zone, calendar invitations, reminders, cancel and reschedule
  links, a JSON slots API, CSV export and a feed of your bookings. Browser slot
  finder demo plus a zero-dependency server with a one-click Render deploy.
stage: prototype
owner: duncan

# Screened 2026-10-16. Paid market is real and proven: Calendly, SavvyCal,
# Acuity, Zoho Bookings and Cal.com charge per seat per month, and a solo
# consultant, tutor, coach or clinic needs a link that offers only free times.
# Open-source schedulers exist (Cal.com, Easy!Appointments) but are full
# platforms with a database and a build; the gap is a one-process scheduler a
# solo operator deploys in a click, with their own calendar as the source of
# truth. Seventh product for the indie-site and small-service buyer of
# support-desk, form-inbox, status-keeper and proposal-maker; a booking link
# is also what a proposal or support reply ends with.
# duplicate_check: grep of ventures/ on 2026-10-16 found only
# appointment-no-show-analyzer, appointment-overbooking-optimizer (calculators),
# booking-request-chooser (rental-night chooser) and tutor-weekly-schedule-optimizer;
# none offers a booking page.
#
# First visitor: people on r/selfhosted, r/Entrepreneur, Hacker News and
# Indie Hackers asking "calendly alternative", "self hosted booking page",
# "calendly free alternative", "cal.com too complicated". Volume not measured
# with an external tool.
#
# Path to revenue (payments stay off): free and MIT as the lead magnet;
# done-for-you setup, a hosted copy under the deployer's own name, or GitHub
# Sponsors are the paid steps; hosting under the public name is owner-gated.

hypotheses:
  - claim: >-
      Solo service providers will deploy their own booking page once it is one
      click and one env var, because per-seat pricing and the feature gating
      of buffers, reminders and several event types is what they resent.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact
  - claim: >-
      Reading their existing calendar's busy time from a secret iCal address,
      with no OAuth app to register, is enough to prevent double-bookings and
      is simpler than the calendar integrations hosted tools sell.
    status: untested
    checked: null
    evidence: customer-contact

economics:
  currency: USD
  mrr: null
  monthly_cost: 0
  customers: null

budget:
  monthly_cap: 1
  protected: false

kill_criteria:
  - Fewer than three distinct GitHub users (issues, stars, or a pasted report) engage within 90 days of the page being reachable from the published site.
  - A report of a double-booked slot, a time shown in the wrong zone, a booking changed or read without its private link, a script injection in the admin or booking pages, or an admin action accepted without the key; correctness, escaping and auth checks come before any new feature.

links:
  production: https://duncan-haywood.github.io/monorepo-projects/slot-keeper/
  analytics: null

fly.toml.text:
# Fly.io self-deploy, in your own account (needs flyctl and a card on file with Fly):
#   fly launch --copy-config --no-deploy --dockerfile Dockerfile
#   fly volumes create state --size 1
#   fly secrets set ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16)
#   (optional settings from render.yaml, e.g. PUBLIC_URL, go in with `fly secrets set` too)
#   fly deploy
# One machine that never auto-stops: the state file lives on its volume.
app = "slot-keeper-CHANGE-ME"
primary_region = "iad"

[build]
  dockerfile = "Dockerfile"

[env]
  PORT = "8080"
  STATE = "/data/state.json"
  TRUST_PROXY = "true"

[mounts]
  source = "state"
  destination = "/data"

[http_service]
  internal_port = 8080
  force_https = true
  auto_stop_machines = "off"
  auto_start_machines = false
  min_machines_running = 1
  [[http_service.checks]]
    path = "/healthz"
    interval = "30s"
    timeout = "5s"

index.html.text:
A booking page you host yourself, with no per-seat fee.

Slot Keeper is the open-source scheduling page for one person or a small team. Set your weekly hours and it offers only the times you are really free, in each visitor's own time zone, then sends the invitation, a reminder, and a link to cancel or reschedule. Below, try the slot finder with your own hours and a pasted calendar. Everything on this page runs in your browser, so nothing is uploaded.

Try the slot finder

The server uses this exact code. Weekly standups from the sample block Monday and Wednesday at 10:00 New York time and keep that time across daylight saving. Slots are measured from the moment you load the page.

Why someone would use this

TodayCatchSlot Keeper
Calendly, SavvyCal, Acuity, Zoho BookingsPriced per seat per month; invitee details live with them; reminders, buffers and multiple event types sit on paid tiersYour server, unlimited event types and bookings, buffers, notice, reminders, no seat fee
Cal.com and other open-source schedulersFull platforms: a database, a build, integrations to configure, real operations workOne Node process and one JSON file; deploys in a click
Back-and-forth email, "what times work?"Slow, easy to double-book, nobody reminds the other side, time zones get muddledOne link; only free times; invitation, reminder and reschedule link included

Honest limits: one host per booking page (no round-robin or team routing), it reads your calendar's busy time but does not write to it (subscribe to the bookings feed), no video-room creation (paste your meeting link), no payments, no mobile app, one admin key. Recurring events use the common rules (daily, weekly with days, monthly, yearly with count or end date); rarer rules count only their first occurrence and the admin page says so.

Run your own copy

Fork the repository, open https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>, and Render builds it in your account with a generated admin key. Or docker compose up anywhere, or Fly.io with the steps in the repository. Add your calendar's secret iCal address as BUSY_ICS_URL and your Resend key to start sending invitations. Nothing runs on the author's accounts.

git clone https://github.com/Duncan-Haywood/oss-monorepo
cd oss-monorepo/ventures/slot-keeper
ADMIN_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) COMPANY_NAME=Acme node server.mjs

Questions

Why not just use Calendly, Cal.com or SavvyCal?

Those are polished and the right call if you need teams with round-robin routing, payments, workflows and a mobile app. Calendly and similar tools charge per seat per month for the features beyond a single basic link, and your invitees' details live on their servers. Slot Keeper is one small Node server in your own account: unlimited event types and bookings, your calendar's busy time respected, invitations with calendar files, reminders and a cancel or reschedule link, with no seat fee. If you are one person or a tiny team that mostly needs a booking link, it covers the job.

How does it know I am busy elsewhere?

Paste your calendar's secret iCal address (Google Calendar, Outlook and Apple Calendar all offer one) into BUSY_ICS_URL. The server reads it every five minutes and never offers a time that overlaps an event, including recurring events, all-day events and different time zones. If the feed cannot be read it keeps the last good copy and warns you on the admin page. It reads busy time only; it does not write to your calendar, so subscribe to the bookings feed it gives you to see bookings there.

Does it handle time zones and daylight saving?

Yes. Your weekly hours are in your zone and each invitee picks theirs; times shift correctly across daylight-saving changes, and a time that does not exist on the spring-forward day is never offered. The demo on this page uses the same code as the server.

How are invitations and reminders sent?

Through your own Resend account with your verified sending domain. It starts in dry-run mode: bookings are saved but no email is sent until you set DRY_RUN=false with RESEND_API_KEY, MAIL_FROM and HOST_EMAIL. Each confirmation carries a calendar file the invitee's app adds to their calendar, and cancelling sends a cancellation file that removes it. A reminder goes out once, a day ahead by default.

Can invitees cancel or reschedule?

Yes. Every booking gets a private link. Rescheduling keeps the old time until the new one is confirmed and then cancels it, so nobody is left with nothing. Only the person who booked, with the right link and email, can change it.

What does it store?

Event types, and each booking's name, email address, optional note and time, in one JSON file you control. IP addresses are held in memory only for rate limiting. Set RETENTION_DAYS to delete old bookings. You are the operator and responsible for your privacy notice and data-protection duties.

Same builder, other jobs: Support Desk answers customer email, Form Inbox collects website forms, Status Keeper runs a public status page and Proposal Maker sends proposals people can accept.

No warranty. This tool and the server are provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind, express or implied, and with no uptime or delivery guarantee. You are the operator of any booking page you run, responsible for the details it collects, a privacy notice, data-protection rules where you and your visitors live, and your own email sending. Check the time and zone of every booking; a missed or double-booked appointment is your responsibility. It is not legal, tax, or financial advice. Everything on this page runs in your browser: nothing you enter is uploaded and the page makes no network requests. Usage counters (opt-out below) stay in your browser's local storage.

render.yaml.text:
# One-click self-deploy: https://render.com/deploy?repo=<your fork URL>
# Render builds the Dockerfile in YOUR account; nothing runs on the author's.
# No third-party key is required to start. BUSY_ICS_URL (your calendar's secret iCal address), ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL (Slack/Discord) and Resend email (HOST_EMAIL, RESEND_API_KEY, MAIL_FROM, DRY_RUN=false) are optional.
services:
  - type: web
    name: slot-keeper
    runtime: docker
    dockerContext: ventures/slot-keeper
    dockerfilePath: ventures/slot-keeper/Dockerfile
    plan: starter
    healthCheckPath: /healthz
    disk:
      name: state
      mountPath: /data
      sizeGB: 1
    envVars:
      - key: STATE
        value: /data/state.json
      - key: TRUST_PROXY
        value: "true"
      - key: ADMIN_KEY
        generateValue: true
      - key: COMPANY_NAME
        sync: false
      - key: ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL
        sync: false
      - key: PUBLIC_URL
        sync: false
      - key: RESEND_API_KEY
        sync: false
      - key: MAIL_FROM
        sync: false
      - key: DRY_RUN
        value: "true"
      - key: BUSY_ICS_URL
        sync: false
      - key: HOST_EMAIL
        sync: false
      - key: DEFAULT_TZ
        value: UTC
      - key: REMINDER_HOURS
        value: "24"
